excerpt: You typed a response as a union. Then you read a field off it and the compiler stopped you. The union is not wrong. The narrowing is missing. A union declares what a value could be. Discrimination decides what it is right now. Multi-type entities show up every day. API responses adopt several shapes. Collections carry several types. Parsed user input collapses to different scalars. Unions describe all of them. For primitives TypeScript does the work alone. A plain if-else narrows the value and the inference follows.
title: On TypeScript discriminated unions
